title: Time-Boxed First Results — Core Method
description: The engine guarantees first results within a time box — say 200 milliseconds — by searching the fastest sources and best indexes first, then continuing in the background. Users see something useful immediately while completeness builds underneath. The time box is a contract: whatever is ready ships, marked as partial, and refinement follows. This responsiveness is why progressive retrieval feels instant even over enormous archives. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.
demo:
import time
deadline = time.time() + 0.05
results, i = [], 0
while time.time() < deadline:
    results.append("r%d" % i); i += 1
print("first results within budget:", results[:3], "... (%d total)" % len(results))

title: Iterative Deepening — Core Method
description: Instead of one exhaustive pass, the engine searches in rounds of increasing depth: quick shallow matches first, then deeper and more expensive sources. Each round's results merge into the running answer, so quality improves monotonically. A round stops early when its marginal gain drops below threshold — diminishing returns are measured, not assumed. Iterative deepening gives users control: stop when satisfied, or let it run to exhaustion. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.
demo:
rounds = [["r1", "r2"], ["r3"], ["r4", "r5"]]
seen = []
for depth, batch in enumerate(rounds, 1):
    seen.extend(batch)
    print("depth %d: %d results so far" % (depth, len(seen)))

title: Streaming Delivery — Core Method
description: Results stream to the user as they are found rather than waiting for the complete set: the engine yields each verified hit the moment it is ready. Streaming composes with ranking — early results are the best-so-far, and later arrivals insert in order. Backpressure keeps a fast producer from overwhelming a slow consumer. For huge result sets, streaming is the only humane interface. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.

title: Early Termination — Core Method
description: Exhaustive search has diminishing returns, so the engine watches the gain curve and stops when new results stop improving the answer. Termination rules combine result novelty, score decay, and elapsed budget into a stop decision made per query. Every early stop is logged with its reason, keeping the behavior auditable. Knowing when to stop is as valuable as knowing where to look. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.

title: Progress Callbacks — Core Method
description: Long searches report progress through callbacks: sources completed, results so far, estimated remaining. Callbacks let interfaces show live progress bars and let orchestrators make mid-search decisions like reallocating budget. The callback payload is a small fixed schema, so any consumer can understand it. Visibility turns waiting from anxiety into information. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.
